system.summary: Bremen 1631: two-digit homophonic substitution, four consecutive numbers per letter, the bands taken down the columns of a six-column alphabet grid, with a small nomenclator of one- and two-digit numbers.
system.notes: Key order: bands of four from 8 taken down the columns of a six-column grid (a g n t / b h o u / c i p w / d k q x / e l r y / f m s z). Describes the Bremen letters only. R4306 (monoalphabetic by IoC, 0.078), R4284 (108 values) and R4282 (about 33 signs, Latin) were not broken; R4333-R4341 were not worked.

prior_solution.where: Interlinear decipherment of about 80% of the Bremen groups, written at the time; DECODE status Partially decrypted

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the 14 DECODE records and their images with the project cookie; found the entry is four unrelated groups (R4282/R4284/R4306 key-box ciphertexts, Bremen 1631, Rusdorff 1628, Oxenstiernska saml. E 708 of June 1633).
Agent transcriptions of R4306 (463 numbers) and R4284 (756 numbers).

Simple-substitution and homophonic annealing of R4306 over quadgram models in nl, de, la, fr, sv, en, it, es, pt, da; first runs collapsed to e/n strings until a search bug (free changes propagating by swaps) and a backoff-model artefact were fixed.
R4306 re-transcribed keeping digit variants (55 tokens); annealed again.
Homophonic Latin annealing of R4284 (8 x 250k), also over 4-number bands.
Fetched 70 Chifferklaver låda II key records; tested the Siebenbürgen key (R4310) and the 1632 key (R4296) on R4306 and R4284.
Bremen letters transcribed with their interlinear glosses.
Aligned glossed words to numbers: four consecutive numbers per letter.
Unglossed bands fixed from unglossed words (k, z, m, w), then the band order recognised as a six-column alphabet grid read by columns, placing q, x and y.
Every cipher group of both Bremen letters decoded (bremen_decoded.txt).
R4282 letter cipher transcribed by agent (33 sign codes).
Homophonic and substitution Latin annealing of R4282, with and without the written word divisions.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The Bremen 1631 band key (R4330-R4331) was rebuilt by aligning the contemporary interlinear glosses (about 80% of groups) with their numbers, then completed from unglossed words and the six-column grid pattern.
outcome.fraction_read_source: _check_profile --measure on the four transcribed documents: bremen_transcription.txt (GLOSS lines removed, --digits) 955 figures, all given a value in bremen_decoded.txt (residue = transcription slips); r4306_v2.txt 465, r4284_transcription.txt 822, r4282_transcription.txt ~1000 signs (letters, [..] clear Latin excluded), all unread; 955/~3240. Rusdorff and E 708 records not in documents[] and not counted
outcome.notes: Bremen 1631 (2 of the 14 records) read in full; R4282, R4284, R4306 attempted and open; Rusdorff 1628 (5) and E 708 June 1633 (4, glossed at the time) not worked. fraction_read 0.3 is measured over the four documents' transcriptions (Bremen 955 figures read of ~3240 cipher tokens); key partial = Bremen band key recovered, none for R4282/R4284/R4306.
